label: Illustrative example: a clinic's consent and record settings: the consent wordings with their versions, who may open a record, the idle lock and how long records are kept.
title: Consent and settings
subtitle: What clients agree to, who may open a record and how long it is kept. A change to a wording makes a new version.

blocks.title: What clients are asked to agree to
rows: I agree to be assessed and treated and for notes to be kept.
I agree that my insurer may receive the information needed for a claim. Nothing is sent without it.
I agree to photos of the treated area being kept in my record. No photo is kept without it.

items.label: The treating practitioner
items.value: Opens their own clients' records with no question

items.label: Other clinical staff
items.value: Must give a reason, which is logged

items.label: Front desk and managers
items.value: Name, phone, bookings and consent state only

items.label: Break-glass
items.value: Anyone clinical, in an emergency, with a written reason; announced at once

items.label: Owner
items.value: The only default role with clinical access

items.label: Adult records
items.value: Kept 7 years after the last visit

items.label: Children's records
items.value: Kept until they turn 18, plus the adult period

items.label: Clients under 18
items.value: Need a guardian; consent is the guardian's

items.label: Privacy officer
items.value: Ayomide Oladipo · applies the retention rules

items.label: Encryption
items.value: Clinical fields encrypted again with this organisation's own key · always on
